subject: physics
title: The Photoelectric Effect
welcome_lead: Shine light on a metal and meet Einstein's photon theory at the work function.
meta_desc: A-Level Quantum adventure on the photoelectric effect and photon energy.
final_note: No emission below the threshold frequency, no matter how bright the light.

concepts.def: Discrete quantum of EM radiation, E = h f.
Minimum energy to free an electron.
½ m v²_max = h f − φ.

walkthroughs.body_html: Each photon delivers energy hf in a single interaction with one electron. If hf > φ, the electron escapes with KE = hf − φ. Intensity controls photon count, not energy.
Below threshold frequency f₀ = φ/h, no electrons are emitted, no matter how intense the light. This killed the wave-only theory of light.
Apply reverse voltage until current stops. Then eV_s = KE_max = hf − φ. Plotting V_s vs f gives a line of gradient h/e.

numericals.q: Photon energy at f = 6 × 10¹⁴ Hz? h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ (×10⁻¹⁹ J)

free_texts.q: What name is given to the minimum energy needed to free an electron from a metal?
